title: Why must online softmax rescale earlier tiles?
scope: Declared scalar worked case for one query: score blocks [1],[3], value blocks [2],[6]. The original HBM ↔ registers/SRAM boundary is retained. Values are toy data, not the chapter’s model workload.

steps.label: Load query tile
steps.description: Keep the query resident on chip. Online state starts with m = −∞, l = 0, a = 0; there is no score-matrix allocation in HBM.

steps.label: Consume first K/V block
steps.description: Temporary on-chip score 1 has weight exp(1−1)=1. The state retains maximum 1, normalization 1, and weighted numerator 2.

steps.label: Rescale and consume block 2
steps.description: The new maximum is 3. Rescale BOTH previous l and a by exp(1−3), then add the new block weight and weighted value. A larger maximum changes the scale, not the represented attention.

steps.label: Normalize after the last block
steps.description: Only after all required blocks, divide retained numerator by normalization. Write the final output; temporary score tiles never become an HBM score matrix.

guard: Invariant: l=Σexp(s−m), a=Σexp(s−m)v over consumed blocks; not a speedup model.
